title: Why P Jayarajan, T V Rajesh were acquitted in Ariyil Shukoor murder case
content: Kochi: The prosecution's failure to establish the alleged criminal conspiracy at the Taliparamba Co-operative Hospital, the non-appearance of crucial witnesses, and gaps in the electronic evidence led to the acquittal of CPM strongman and the party's then Kannur district secretary P Jayarajan and former Kalliasseri MLA T V Rajesh in the 2012 Ariyil Shukoor murder case. The Additional Special Sessions Court (CBI)-III, Ernakulam, found that the prosecution had failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt that Jayarajan and Rajesh- the last two accused in the list of 33 accused- were part of a conspiracy to murder Muslim Students Federation (MSF) activist Abdul Shukoor Ariyil and attempt to murder his friend P Sakkariya. The two leaders had been accused of being part of a conspiracy allegedly hatched at Room 315 of the Taliparamba Co-operative Hospital on February 20, 2012, where they were admitted after their vehicle was attacked by suspected Muslim League activists at Ariyil in Pattavum grama panchayat near Taliparamba. The prosecution alleged that CPM leaders and activists had gathered at the hospital and conspired to eliminate those involved in the attack on Jayarajan and Rajesh. It further alleged that the two leaders knew about the plan to murder Shukoor but concealed it without informing the authorities. Kerala police had initially charged the two leaders under Section 118 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), accusing them of knowing about the alleged plan to kill Shukoor but not stopping it. The CBI subsequently filed a supplementary chargesheet accusing them of criminal conspiracy under Section 120B read with Sections 364 (kidnapping or abducting in order to murder), 307 (attempt to murder) and 302 (murder) of the IPC. The court, while framing charges on October 18, 2024, held that Section 120B was prima facie attracted and that there was no need to frame a separate charge under Section 118. Key witnesses did not turn up In its examination of the alleged conspiracy, the court noted that the prosecution had cited P P Abu (CW22), Mohammed Swabir (CW23), Divakaran (CW40) and M K Manoharan (CW41) to establish the alleged conspiracy at the hospital. The CBI, in its supplementary final report, had also cited four witnesses – Vasudevan (CW15), Pramod (CW16), Rajesh (CW17) and Mukundan (CW18) to prove the same charges. Of the eight witnesses, only M K Manoharan, a reporter with Makthab, an evening daily at Taliparamba, turned up. P P Abu and Mohammed Swabir went abroad, and their presence could not be secured despite repeated warrants. Vasudevan was reported dead. The prosecution gave up on Rajesh, Mukundan, Divakaran and Pramod, who was the personal security officer of Jayarajan at the time. The court noted that the prosecution had thus failed to examine almost all the witnesses it had cited to establish the alleged conspiracy. Journalist's testimony helped the defence The testimony of Manoharan, the journalist, proved significant in the acquittal. Manoharan had reported on the CPM-Muslim League clash at Ariyil on February 19, 2012. He went to Ariyil again on February 20 after receiving information that suspected Muslim League workers had painted the red office of the CPM green at Ariyil. He testified that Jayarajan, the then CPM Kannur district secretary, Rajesh, the then Kalliasseri MLA, and other leaders had reached the place. Their vehicle was attacked and destroyed, leaving Jayarajan, Rajesh, Deshabhimani reporter Rajeevan and CPM area committee member Balakrishnan injured. Manoharan followed them to the Taliparamba Co-operative Hospital, where Jayarajan and Rajesh were admitted to Room 315. He testified that several CPM leaders and activists, including former MLA K K Shylaja, C N Chandran, U Babu Gopinath, T K Govindan (now a UDF MLA) and former MLA C N Krishnan, visited the two leaders. During cross-examination, he said several people had assembled at the hospital following the attack and police officers were also on duty there...
